contentEn:
Bathroom renovations in Vancouver cost $10,000–$60,000 in 2026; kitchen renovations run $15,000–$80,000 or more. The short answer to which you should do first: if your bathrooms are functionally broken — leaking, mouldy, or inaccessible — fix those first. If all bathrooms work but your kitchen is dated, start with the kitchen. Here is how the costs, timelines and resale value compare across the two rooms, using real data from Reno Stars' Vancouver-area projects.

Kitchen vs Bathroom Renovation Cost in Vancouver (2026)

Across Reno Stars' completed projects, here is what Vancouver homeowners actually paid in 2026:

Project TypeCost Range (CAD)Timeline
Bathroom — cosmetic refresh$10,000–$22,0003–5 weeks
Bathroom — mid-range gut$25,000–$45,0006–10 weeks
Bathroom — premium/custom$50,000–$60,000+10–16 weeks
Kitchen — cosmetic/partial$15,000–$35,0004–8 weeks
Kitchen — mid-range gut$40,000–$65,0008–14 weeks
Kitchen — premium/custom$70,000–$80,000+12–20 weeks

Labour accounts for 45–65% of both kitchen and bathroom budgets. Material costs run higher per square foot in bathrooms because waterproofing, tiling and plumbing rough-in are more labour-intensive than typical kitchen work. Kitchens cost more in absolute terms because they are larger and require more cabinetry, appliances and countertop area.

Which Renovation Has Higher Resale Value in Vancouver?

Both rooms deliver strong resale value, but the numbers favour kitchens slightly for gross dollar return and bathrooms for percentage return on investment. A mid-range kitchen renovation in Vancouver adds approximately $35,000–$55,000 in assessed value, according to renovation industry cost-value analysis from the Vancouver market. A mid-range bathroom renovation adds $22,000–$38,000. The kitchen wins on absolute dollar gain; the bathroom wins if you are working with a tighter budget relative to the investment.

For context, Reno Stars' Vancouver whole house renovation project — a 1,800 sq ft detached home in Vancouver — included both kitchen and bathroom updates and added measurable resale premium across the full project scope.

When to Do the Bathroom Before the Kitchen

Do the bathroom first if any of the following apply: there is active water leakage; mould is visible; the layout makes the space unsafe or inaccessible for an older family member; or the bathroom has original plumbing from before 1990 that is approaching failure. These are not cosmetic concerns — they are liability issues that reduce home value if unaddressed.

A practical refresh that fixes function while adding modern finishes typically costs $18,000–$28,000 in Vancouver. Reno Stars' two-bathroom renovation in Burnaby — with custom features and upgraded waterproofing — illustrates what a mid-range Vancouver bathroom gut looks like in practice.

When to Do the Kitchen Before the Bathroom

Do the kitchen first if the kitchen is the primary pain point — dated cabinets, worn countertops, poor layout — and all existing bathrooms are functional, dry and free of mould. For most Vancouver families, the kitchen is the highest-traffic room in the home and the most visible to guests. A kitchen refresh also anchors the aesthetic of adjacent rooms, making a later bathroom feel more cohesive if you do both.

Reno Stars' custom kitchen renovation in Burnaby — featuring wood-vein quartz countertops, matte black fixtures, and custom shaker cabinets — shows the premium result possible with a well-executed Vancouver kitchen project.

Can You Do Both at the Same Time?

Yes, but the budget required is significant: a simultaneous kitchen and primary bathroom gut in Vancouver typically runs $70,000–$130,000 all-in. Reno Stars' custom whole house renovation in Vancouver included both a full kitchen and primary bathroom gut alongside flooring, exterior updates and structural work — illustrating how a coordinated whole-home approach manages disruption better than two separate projects.

If budget allows and you are staying in the home for five or more years, doing both at once typically saves 8–12% versus running them sequentially, because site setup, trades mobilization and permit fees are shared across one project instead of two.

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation in Vancouver? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a bathroom reno worth it in Vancouver in 2026?

Yes — a mid-range bathroom renovation in Vancouver typically costs $25,000–$45,000 and adds $22,000–$38,000 in resale value, a return of 85–95%. Premium bathroom renovations ($50,000–$60,000+) yield a lower percentage return but substantially improve daily quality of life and buyer appeal in a competitive market.

What costs the most in a Vancouver kitchen renovation?

Cabinetry and countertops together account for 40–55% of a Vancouver kitchen renovation budget. Appliances add another 10–15%. Labour (electrical, plumbing, tiling, general contracting) makes up 45–65% of the total, depending on scope and whether structural changes are involved.

How long does a bathroom renovation take in Vancouver?

A cosmetic bathroom refresh takes 3–5 weeks. A mid-range gut renovation takes 6–10 weeks. A premium custom bathroom with structural or plumbing changes takes 10–16 weeks. Permit processing in Vancouver adds 4–8 weeks on top if structural or plumbing work is involved — plan accordingly when setting a move-in or listing date.

Should I do the kitchen or bathroom first if I only have budget for one?

If all bathrooms are functional and dry, do the kitchen first — it generates higher absolute resale value and has more daily impact on your quality of life. If any bathroom has active water issues, mould or failing plumbing, address that before spending on the kitchen.

Does renovating the kitchen add more value than the bathroom in Vancouver?

In absolute dollars, yes — a mid-range kitchen renovation in Vancouver typically adds $35,000–$55,000 in assessed value versus $22,000–$38,000 for a mid-range bathroom. As a percentage of renovation cost, bathrooms slightly edge kitchens. For most Vancouver homeowners, the kitchen wins on both metrics if budget allows only one project.

For more Vancouver renovation cost data, see Reno Stars' Kitchen Renovation Cost Guide and Bathroom Renovation Cost Guide.

2026年温哥华卫生间装修费用为$10,000至$60,000；厨房装修为$15,000至$80,000或更高。简答：应先进行哪一项？如果卫生间功能损坏——漏水、发霉或无障碍设施不完善——优先修复。如果所有卫生间功能正常但厨房陈旧，则从厨房开始。以下是聚星装修基于温哥华地区真实项目数据，对两个房间的费用、时间表和转售价值的详细对比。

温哥华厨房vs卫生间装修费用（2026年）

根据聚星装修已完成的温哥华地区项目，以下是2026年温哥华业主的实际支出：

项目类型费用范围（加元）工期
卫生间——美容翻新$10,000–$22,0003–5周
卫生间——中档整体翻新$25,000–$45,0006–10周
卫生间——高档定制$50,000–$60,000+10–16周
厨房——美容/局部翻新$15,000–$35,0004–8周
厨房——中档整体翻新$40,000–$65,0008–14周
厨房——高档定制$70,000–$80,000+12–20周

人工费用占厨房和卫生间预算的45%至65%。每平方英尺的材料费用方面，卫生间高于厨房，因为防水、瓷砖铺贴和管道工程比典型厨房工作更耗人工。厨房的绝对费用更高，因为面积更大，需要更多橱柜、家电和台面区域。

温哥华装修——哪种装修转售价值更高？

两个房间都能带来强劲的转售价值，但数字上厨房略胜绝对金额，卫生间略胜投资回报率百分比。温哥华中档厨房装修可使评估价值增加约$35,000至$55,000。中档卫生间装修可增加$22,000至$38,000。厨房在绝对金额上胜出；如果按预算与投资的比例计算，卫生间胜出。

作为参考，聚星装修的温哥华整屋装修项目——一套1,800平方英尺的独立屋——包括厨房和卫生间更新，在整个项目范围内增加了可衡量的转售溢价。

什么时候应先装修卫生间

如果存在以下情况，应先装修卫生间：存在活跃的漏水；可见霉斑；布局使空间对老年家庭成员不安全或无法使用；或者卫生间有1990年以前的原始管道，接近故障状态。这些不是美观问题——它们是如果不予处理会降低房屋价值的责任问题。

修复功能同时添加现代饰面的实用翻新在温哥华通常花费$18,000至$28,000。聚星装修的本拿比双卫生间装修项目——配有定制功能和升级防水——展示了一个中档温哥华卫生间整体翻新的实际情况。

什么时候应先装修厨房

如果厨房是主要痛点——橱柜陈旧、台面磨损、布局不佳——且所有现有卫生间功能正常，则先装修厨房。对大多数温哥华家庭来说，厨房是家中流量最高的房间，也是对客人最可见的空间。厨房翻新也为相邻房间的美学定调，如果后续再做卫生间，会感觉更加协调。

聚星装修的本拿比定制厨房装修项目——配木纹石英台面、哑光黑色五金件和定制橱柜——展示了精心执行的温哥华厨房项目所能达到的高档效果。

可以同时进行两项装修吗？

可以，但所需预算相当可观：温哥华同时进行厨房和主卫整体翻新的费用通常为$70,000至$130,000全包。聚星装修的温哥华定制整屋装修项目包括全套厨房和主卫翻新，以及地板、外部更新和结构工程——说明了一体化的整屋方案比两个独立项目更好地管理施工干扰。

如果预算允许且您计划在该房屋居住五年或更长时间，一次性完成两项通常比顺序进行节省8%至12%，因为场地准备、人工调配和许可费用是一次性分摊，而不是分两次支付。

计划在温哥华进行厨房、卫生间、整屋或商业装修？立即获取聚星装修的免费、无约束报价。

常见问题

2026年在温哥华进行卫生间装修值得吗？

值得——温哥华中档卫生间装修通常花费$25,000至$45,000，可增加$22,000至$38,000的转售价值，回报率为85%至95%。高档卫生间装修（$50,000至$60,000+）的百分比回报率较低，但实质性地改善了日常生活品质和在竞争激烈的市场中的买家吸引力。

温哥华厨房装修中哪项费用最高？

橱柜和台面合计占温哥华厨房装修预算的40%至55%。家电另占10%至15%。人工（电气、管道、瓷砖、装修总包）占总额的45%至65%，具体取决于工程范围以及是否有结构变更。

温哥华卫生间装修需要多长时间？

美容卫生间翻新需3至5周。中档整体翻新需6至10周。有结构或管道变更的高档定制卫生间需10至16周。如果涉及结构或管道工程，许可处理在温哥华另需4至8周——在设定入住或挂牌日期时相应规划。

如果预算只够一项，应该先装修厨房还是卫生间？

如果所有卫生间功能正常且干燥，先装修厨房——它产生更高的绝对转售价值，对日常生活影响也更大。如果任何卫生间存在活跃的漏水问题、霉斑或管道故障，应在厨房之前先处理。

在温哥华，厨房装修是否比卫生间装修增值更多？

按绝对金额计算，是的——温哥华中档厨房装修通常使评估价值增加$35,000至$55,000，而中档卫生间增加$22,000至$38,000。作为装修成本的百分比，卫生间略胜厨房。对大多数温哥华业主来说，如果预算只允许一个项目，厨房在两个指标上都胜出。

了解更多温哥华装修费用数据，请参阅聚星装修的厨房装修费用指南和卫生间装修费用指南。
